_lane: L4 — stackup and fabrication, halo Replica
_convention: FRONT = the component side, per Apple's FCC filing (A2187 internal photos label it 'MLB - Front'). Colin O'Flynn calls that same face 'backside'. Every side reference below is Apple's.
_the_rule_this_file_exists_to_enforce: WHAT APPLE DID and WHAT WE CAN MAKE are two different facts and are never merged into one row. The Replica is the reference the other five variants are measured against; if it is drawn at whatever a process happens to allow, the reference has already diverged and every downstream comparison silently inherits that divergence.
_owns: the board in the third dimension: layers, thickness, materials, finish, and what a real fabricator will build. NOT the outline, NOT the centre hole, NOT any diameter — those are lane L1.

apple._what: The AirTag as built by Apple. Every row carries the input it came from.

board_thickness_mm.source: Colin O'Flynn, Twitter/X, quoted in research/fetched/A-oflynn-testpoints-and-glitch-repos.md line 22: "it's 0.3mm PCB so I'm pretty sure I broke some solder joints getting it out."
board_thickness_mm.source_kind: a teardown engineer's statement in passing, not a caliper reading
board_thickness_mm.corroboration: Adam Catley, independently: "Removing the PCB is likely to cause damage due to the thin PCB and being soldered to the plastic tray." — research/fetched/G-teardown-mechanical-quotes.md. This corroborates THIN. It does not corroborate 0.30.
board_thickness_mm.uncertainty: unbounded downward and upward. No error bar was ever published with it.
board_thickness_mm.attempted_and_failed: Direct measurement from photographs. No published photograph shows the board edge-on. FCC internal photo 6 is the best-scaled frame at 15.887 px/mm (L1, docs/REFERENCE-TEARDOWN.md), where 0.30 mm spans 4.8 px and the board lies flat — nothing to measure. O'Flynn's backside scan at ~90-110 px/mm would resolve 0.30 mm as 27-33 px, but it is also flat-on.
board_thickness_mm.what_would_settle_it: a caliper on a real bare MLB, or a scale-referenced edge-on photograph, or a cross-section micrograph.

layer_count.verdict: COUNTED — from a published physical delayering of an AirTag board
layer_count._this_supersedes: the CANNOT DETERMINE that stood in docs/REFERENCE-TEARDOWN.md §3 and §7, and the narrowed-to-[4,6] recorded in this file at commit 98c6663. §3's own words were 'never published. Likely 4.' It WAS published — in a form the dossier read as carrying no count.

layer_count.the_question_that_had_to_be_answered_fir: Whether each file is ONE delayered copper layer or a SUPERPOSITION of all of them. docs/REFERENCE-TEARDOWN.md took 'merged' to mean superposition, which would make four files carry no count at all. The readings make opposite predictions at one board spot: under superposition a feature on any layer appears in EVERY image; under delayering it appears in one and is ABSENT from the others.

the_test_and_its_result.spot: the fine-pitch square land grid on layer1 at box [1330,1080,1600,1330], and the SAME board location on the others at box [845,686,1017,845] (layers 2-4 are 1280 px wide against layer1's 2014, so the box is scaled, not moved)
the_test_and_its_result.layer1: a square land grid of component pads with fanout traces running out of it — a feature only an OUTER layer can carry
the_test_and_its_result.layer2_at_the_same_spot: NO land grid. Round via lands linked by thin traces cut out of a copper field — an inner layer
the_test_and_its_result.conclusion: The grid is absent where superposition requires it to be present. These are four separate physical layers.

what_each_layer_shows.layer1: OUTER, component side. Dense fine routing, component footprints, a fine-pitch land grid consistent with the nRF52832 WLCSP, a second land array, three plated tooling/clip holes.
what_each_layer_shows.layer2: INNER. Largely a copper pour with antipads and isolated islands, light routing, a cross-shaped fiducial. Plane-like.
what_each_layer_shows.layer3: INNER. Long parallel routed traces running around the annulus, a pour region on one side, the same fiducial. Routing-like.
what_each_layer_shows.layer4: OUTER, the other face. Large round pads consistent with battery contacts and bulk capacitors, a small dense footprint, no fine land grid.

why_the_set_is_read_as_complete: The sequence is STRUCTURALLY CLOSED: outer-with-pads, inner, inner, outer-with-pads. A missing layer would have to be an inner one.
All four share the same board outline, the same centre hole and the same three plated tooling holes at the same positions — one board, successively ground down, at consistent registration.
The author's own README says 'all the layers'.
Each image carries features the others do not, which is what rules out superposition.
layer_count.independent_corroboration: Two lines derived BEFORE these images were found — the arithmetic and the routing argument were committed at 98c6663, timestamped, so neither can have been fitted to this evidence. The thickness arithmetic gives AT MOST 4 for rigid FR-4 in 0.30 mm; the routing argument gives MORE THAN 2. Both brackets close on 4. Three independent lines agreeing is what a real confirmation looks like.
what_is_still_not_known: WHICH board was delayered. The repo does not say whether it was production 820-01736-A or the FCC sample 920-08283-01. Whether those two share a stackup remains CANNOT DETERMINE and is not assumed.
Whether the vias are all through-holes or include blind/buried ones. Not tested. This bears on whether the build is HDI and on the copper weights, neither of which this finding settles.
The delayering was done by one person on one unit. It has not been independently repeated.
layer_count.what_would_overturn_it: A cross-section showing copper layers the delayering did not photograph, or the author stating the set is incomplete. Note that a 6-layer board would additionally have to be an ultra-thin HDI build to fit 0.30 mm — the arithmetic and this count would both have to be wrong together.
instruments_built_for_this_and_REJECTED: FFT periodicity probe. A land grid is periodic; a pour is not. REJECTED because its negative control went red: blank off-board background scored 10.55 against the real land grid's 8.28 — HIGHER. On a flat patch the whole band sits near zero so one JPEG-noise bin towers over the average. Adding detrending and a median baseline made every patch, background included, return the lowest bin at a round 32.0 px. Abandoned rather than tuned: tuning a threshold until the answer comes out right is the defect, not the fix.

Edge-density probe. Its controls DO pass — blank background 0.0153 and 0.0294 against 0.2541 to 0.4684 for any patch of board, better than tenfold. But it cannot separate a land grid (0.4684) from ordinary inner-layer routing (0.2541-0.3492); that is one continuum, not two categories. KEPT as tools/s_layerprobe.py, which exits 2 on the superposition question and says so. Its honest contribution is the negative control: it proves the compared patches all hold real copper rather than blank photograph, which is the one way the visual reading could have been trivially wrong.
What actually settled it was the eye on named, reproducible crops. Recorded because an automated instrument was tried twice and neither earned the answer.

construction_type.verdict: CONSISTENT WITH THE PHOTOGRAPH, not proven
construction_type.evidence: The routed board edge in O'Flynn's backside scan shows a pale yellow-cream line under the dark soldermask, which is the colour of a cut glass-fibre laminate edge. A polyimide flex core cut edge is amber-translucent and a solid dark material would show no such line.

ruled_out_and_why.flex_or_rigid_flex: considered because 0.30 mm sits in flex territory and because a flexible board would make the 6-layer branch easy. Discarded as the primary hypothesis on the yellow laminate edge above, and because the board carries a shield can, a 50-ball WLCSP and 5 bulk capacitors — a component load that is not put on flex without a stiffener, and no stiffener appears in any photograph. NOT discarded as a possibility for an ultra-thin core INSIDE a rigid stack.

surface_finish.value: gold-bearing — ENIG or another immersion/electroless-gold finish
surface_finish.method: tools/s_colour.py on images/airtag/oflynn-backside-fullres.jpeg. Hue of the plated hole rims against the hue of the bare copper wire of a wirewound inductor IN THE SAME FRAME, under the same light. Colour under an unknown illuminant cannot be trusted absolutely; a hue DIFFERENCE between two metals in one frame survives a white-balance error because the error moves both together. That is why the control is not optional.
surface_finish.result: 19-22 degrees of hue separation between the plated rims and known bare copper in the same frame. The rims are not copper and not OSP-over-copper. They are not HASL or immersion tin or immersion silver either, all of which are grey — R, G and B within a few counts of each other, no warm pixels at all.
surface_finish.still_cannot_determine: WHICH gold finish. ENIG, ENEPIG, immersion gold and hard gold are indistinguishable by hue in a JPEG. A cross-section or XRF would separate them.
surface_finish.supporting_inference_labelled_as_such: A 50-ball WLCSP and 0201 passives need a coplanar finish. HASL cannot hold coplanarity at that scale. This agrees with the measurement but was NOT used to reach it.

soldermask_colour.bounded_to: dark and neutral — not green, not blue, not red, not white
soldermask_colour.measurement: flat mask patches in O'Flynn's backside scan read V=65 to 128 against a white background CONTROL at V=224 in the same frame, with R, G and B within about 10 counts of each other.
soldermask_colour.why_not_closed: A JPEG under an unknown illuminant and unknown camera white balance cannot separate black from matte black from a very dark blue or purple. The apparent violet cast (hue ~270 deg at saturation 0.14) is within what a white-balance error produces on a near-neutral dark surface, so it is not evidence of a purple mask.
soldermask_colour.what_would_settle_it: the board photographed beside a colour checker, or in hand.

silkscreen.evidence: The legend '820-01736-A' and data code '2920 17' are legible as light-on-dark in O'Flynn's front-side scan (images/airtag/oflynn-frontside-tpnames.jpg, catalogued in images/airtag/CATALOG.md). On a dark mask, legible legend is white.

copper_weight.why: Copper weight is a thickness, and no photograph of this board shows a thickness. Nothing in any teardown states it.
copper_weight.what_would_settle_it: a cross-section, or a fabrication drawing.

board_part_numbers._warning: THESE ARE TWO DIFFERENT BOARDS AND ARE NOT MERGED. docs/REFERENCE-TEARDOWN.md §7 lists 'whether the FCC-sample board differs electrically from production' as an open question, and it is still open.

production.reading: Apple's 820-xxxxx-x series is a main-logic-board number; the trailing -A is a revision letter.

fcc_sample.reading: A different Apple number series and a 2019 data code against the production board's 2020. This is an earlier engineering build, not the same board with a second marking.

board_part_numbers.consequence_for_this_lane: Every stackup fact here is drawn from photographs of the PRODUCTION board (O'Flynn's scans) except where an FCC photo is named. Whether the FCC sample shares its stackup is CANNOT DETERMINE and is not assumed.

antennas_and_the_stackup.finding: The BLE and UWB antennas are NOT in board copper — they are on the plastic carrier. L1 tested the opposite hypothesis against O'Flynn's backside scan at ~90-110 px/mm and refuted it: no meander, no inverted-F, no patch in the outer copper of either face. See docs/REFERENCE-TEARDOWN.md §2.3 and evidence/E01-ARE-THE-ANTENNAS-ON-THE-BOARD.md, commit 52d2931.
antennas_and_the_stackup.why_it_matters_here: It removes an antenna-clearance constraint on the stackup — no layer has to be kept clear under an on-board radiator. It does NOT remove the reference-plane requirement: the feeds still cross the board to reach the rim joints, and that is part of the lower-bound argument above.

replica_as_drawn._what: What the halo Replica is DRAWN as. This is a decision, not a measurement, and it was settled with the halo lane which owns the variants table.
replica_as_drawn.decision: Draw the Replica at 0.30 mm as-drawn and record the fabrication delta separately.
replica_as_drawn.reasoning: The Replica is the reference against which the other five variants are measured. Drawing it at whatever a process happens to allow would move the reference itself, and every downstream comparison would silently inherit that divergence without any document recording that it happened.
replica_as_drawn.finish_note: Chosen because the measurement says gold-bearing and because a 50-ball WLCSP needs coplanarity. ENIG is the specific member of the family that both prototype houses offer.
replica_as_drawn.soldermask_note: The measurement bounds Apple's mask to 'dark and neutral' and cannot go finer. Black is the nearest orderable colour to that bound at both houses and is recorded as a CHOICE within the measured bound, not as Apple's colour.
replica_as_drawn.layer_count_basis: MATCHES APPLE, and is no longer a Replica assumption. The orchestrator authorised drawing at 4 as our own choice within the [4,6] bound while Apple's stayed unknown; the delayering evidence arrived in the same session and made that unnecessary. The Replica is drawn at 4 because the AirTag is 4. If the count is ever overturned, this row moves with it — it is not an independent decision that would survive the evidence changing.

fabrication_delta._what: WHAT WE CAN MAKE. Read off published capability pages only. No account was created, no quote was requested, nobody was contacted, no money was spent.
fabrication_delta._and_what_it_does_not_mean: Nothing about Apple. These are prototype houses. Apple's suppliers build at volumes and tolerances no prototype capability page describes. A capability page bounds what WE can order; it does not bound what Apple built.

pcbway.verdict_for_0_30mm: 0.30 mm is NOT one of the listed options at any layer count. It falls between 0.2 and 0.4. At 2 layers it is inside the stated 0.2 mm floor and might be a non-standard-review item; at 4 layers it is BELOW the 0.40 mm floor and is not orderable.
pcbway.moq: CANNOT DETERMINE — no prototype MOQ is published on the capabilities page, and finding one would require the ordering flow. Not pursued: no accounts, no quotes.

jlcpcb.verdict_for_0_30mm: 0.30 mm is below JLCPCB's overall minimum at ANY layer count. Not orderable.

four_layer_thickness_row.method: JLCPCB's live quote configurator, by ce-workshop-9a. At 4 layers the Thickness row offers 0.8/1.0/1.2/1.6/2.0 and GREYS OUT 0.4 and 0.6.
four_layer_thickness_row.negative_control: clicking 0.4 at 4 layers does nothing — the selection stays on 1.6
four_layer_thickness_row.positive_control: switching 4 -> 2 layers RE-ENABLES 0.4 in the same page with no reload, so the disable tracks layer count and is a real constraint rather than styling
four_layer_thickness_row.why_this_row_matters: it is the row this lane had recorded as UNVERIFIED and then reasoned past — see the correction below

fabrication_delta.the_delta_in_one_line: 0.30 mm as-drawn is not orderable from either house at any layer count above two, and not from JLCPCB at any layer count at all. Building a Replica board therefore requires either an HDI house whose capability page was not read, or a stated departure from as-drawn.

the_departure_if_one_is_needed.status: SUPERSEDES this lane's earlier proposal of 0.40 mm, WHICH WAS WRONG
the_departure_if_one_is_needed.the_error_and_it_was_mine: This lane proposed 0.40 mm as 'the nearest orderable thickness above 0.30 AT BOTH HOUSES'. That claim was unsupported for JLCPCB at 4 layers, and the row that would have caught it is the one THIS FILE had already marked UNVERIFIED — recorded as a caveat and then reasoned past in the very next field. 0.4 and 0.6 are not offered at 4 layers. PCBWay's 0.40 four-layer floor stands; the 'both houses' half did not.
the_departure_if_one_is_needed.why_0_80: the thinnest thickness JLCPCB offers at 4 layers, measured in the live configurator with both controls (see the jlcpcb row above)
the_departure_if_one_is_needed.and_the_rule: 0.80 mm is a fact about US, not about Apple. The as-drawn 0.30 mm does not move, and the two numbers stay side by side. Collapsing them is the failure THE-DRIFT.md is about.

discarded.hypothesis: The AirTag board is 4 layers, because 4 is plausible for a board like this.
discarded.why_discarded: Discarded AS A REASON, while the number turned out to be right. §3 said 'likely 4' with nothing behind it, and this lane refused to adopt it and recorded [4,6] instead. The count is now 4 on a physical delayering. A guess that happens to land on the truth is still a guess, and had the answer been 6 the plausibility argument would have written the wrong number into every downstream document permanently. The reasoning is what was wrong; keeping the distinction is the point.

It is plausible and it is unsourced. §3 of the dossier says 'likely 4' and no primary source says 4. The arithmetic makes 4 the only rigid-FR-4 answer, which is a CONDITIONAL result and not the same statement. Recorded as narrowed-to-[4,6], never as 4.

discarded.hypothesis: Six or more layers, from the density of the board.
discarded.why_discarded: Not discarded — narrowed. 6 is excluded in rigid FR-4 by 0.350 mm of dielectric alone against a 0.30 mm target; it survives only in an ultra-thin HDI build whose material data was not obtained. 8 and above are excluded outright: 0.622 mm of laminate at the thin end of stocked material.

discarded.hypothesis: Board thickness can be measured off a photograph.
discarded.why_discarded: No published photograph shows the board edge-on, and the best-scaled flat frame renders 0.30 mm as 4.8 px. Discarded on the resolution arithmetic, not on a failed attempt to eyeball it.

discarded.hypothesis: Antennas etched in board copper would constrain which layers can be ground.
discarded.why_discarded: L1 refuted the premise: no antenna structure exists in the outer copper of either face. The reference-plane requirement for the feed traces survives; the clearance requirement does not.

discarded.hypothesis: Soldermask is purple, from its measured hue of ~270 degrees.
discarded.why_discarded: Saturation is 0.14 on a near-neutral dark surface, which is inside what an unknown camera white balance produces. Reporting purple would be reading a camera setting as a material property.

discarded.hypothesis: A prototype house's minimum thickness tells us what Apple could build.
discarded.why_discarded: It tells us what WE can order. Apple's suppliers are not prototype houses. Fusing the two is the specific error this file's two-column structure exists to prevent.

discarded.hypothesis: 'Merged PCB pictures of all the layers' means a superposition, so the four files carry no count.
discarded.why_discarded: This was the dossier's reading and it was wrong. Tested at a named spot: layer1's land grid is ABSENT from layer2 at the same board location. 'Merged' means each image is stitched from several shots of ONE layer, not that the layers are merged together. Recorded because a single word read the wrong way kept this question open for two days.

open_and_escalated.item: Whether the vias are all through-holes, or include blind/buried ones
open_and_escalated.why_it_matters: It decides whether the build is ordinary 4-layer or HDI, which in turn bears on the copper weights and on whether 0.30 mm was comfortable or aggressive for Apple.
open_and_escalated.cheapest_next_step: compare via land positions between layer1 and layer4 in the delayering set. A land on one outer face with no counterpart on the other is a blind via. That is a registration problem on images already in hand — real work, not an escalation.

open_and_escalated.settles_outright: a caliper on a bare MLB.

open_and_escalated.state: CANNOT DETERMINE within the gold family

open_and_escalated.item: Whether the FCC-sample board 920-08283-01 shares the production board's stackup
open_and_escalated.settles_outright: comparing a 2019 EVT unit to a retail unit.

tools.s_stackup_budget.py: the layer-count arithmetic. Verbs: doctor, budget, bounds, selftest. Exit code IS the verdict — 0 PASS, 1 FAIL, 2 CANNOT DETERMINE. Never takes a layer count as an input to be confirmed. 9 selftest cases, all watched to go red on purpose.
tools.s_colour.py: hue of a metal region against an in-frame control. Refuses a box with no warm pixels rather than averaging shadow.
tools.s_crop.py: crop and Lanczos-upscale. No sharpening, no contrast stretch, no gamma.
tools.s_layerprobe.py: the superposition test's instrumentation. Verbs: structure, selftest. Exits 2 on the layer question BY DESIGN — it can prove the compared patches hold copper rather than blank photograph, which is the negative control on the visual reading, and it cannot separate a land grid from routing. Its docstring records the FFT probe that was rejected when its own negative control went red.

fab_as_ordered._what: What the FAB BRANCH is ordered as. A DIFFERENT KIND OF OBJECT from replica_as_drawn, and the distinction is the point:
fab_as_ordered._pcb_branch: pcb/ is a TRANSCRIPTION. It must equal Apple: 0.30 mm. Measured against replica_as_drawn.
fab_as_ordered._fab_branch: fab/ is a BUILDABLE DEPARTURE. Every departure is enumerated in fab/README.md. Measuring it against as-drawn would fail forever, and a permanent expected-red is a check people learn to ignore.
fab_as_ordered._why_this_is_not_a_tautology: A lane inventing the spec it is then measured against agrees with itself. So this row does NOT record 'whatever the board says' — it records the VENDOR'S OFFER LIST, which is external and can contradict us. s_stackup_budget.py verify --spec as-ordered checks THREE things separately: (1) the SPEC ITSELF must be orderable at its own layer count, which is the guard against inventing a convenient number; (2) the BOARD must be orderable; (3) the board must equal the spec. Setting either the board or the spec to 0.5 mm makes it fail harder, not pass.

vendor_offer.source: live quote configurator, measured 2026-09-05 by ce-workshop-9a with a negative control (0.4 at 4 layers does nothing) and a positive control (4 -> 2 layers re-enables 0.4 in the same page)

fab_as_ordered._apples_number_is_untouched: Apple's board is 0.30 mm reported and 4 layers COUNTED. Nothing here changes either.
